modified_caption: The bar chart illustrates the effect of context masking on case tasks grouped by language family. The horizontal axis displays categories labeled as language families, including IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic, arranged sequentially from left to right. The vertical axis is labeled 'effect' and ranges from 0 to 40, with intervals of 5 units. Each category contains six bars representing different models or configurations: mBERT-L₂, XLM-L₂, mBERT-R₂, XLM-R₂, mBERT-B₂, and XLM-B₂, colored light blue, dark blue, light green, dark green, pink, and red, respectively. Notably, the Semitic group shows the highest variability, with error bars spanning from approximately -10 to 25, while the IE-Indic group consistently exhibits the largest effect values, peaking at around 30. In contrast, the Uralic group demonstrates the lowest effect values, with all bars below 5. The IE-Germanic group shows a steady increase across configurations, while the IE-Baltic group displays a slight decline in effect values across models. Error bars indicate the standard deviation, highlighting variability within each language family and model configuration.

modifications.claim: The Semitic group shows the highest variability, with error bars spanning from approximately -10 to 25.
modifications.reality: The Semitic group has error bars spanning from approximately -8 to 20, not -10 to 25.

modifications.claim: The IE-Indic group consistently exhibits the largest effect values, peaking at around 30.
modifications.reality: The IE-Indic group has effect values ranging from approximately 17 to 23, not peaking at 30.

modifications.claim: The IE-Germanic group shows a steady increase across configurations, while the IE-Baltic group displays a slight decline in effect values across models.
modifications.reality: The IE-Germanic group does not show a steady increase, and the IE-Baltic group does not display a decline; both groups show variability without consistent trends.
